गर्मी और उमस से लोगों को काफी हद तक राहत मिली है. मौसम विभाग के मुताबिक एक साइक्लोनिक सर्कुलेशन और लो प्रेशर एरिया की वजह से प्रदेश में मानसून फिर से एक्टिव हो गया है. इसका प्रभाव सरगुजा और बिलासपुर संभाग में अगले चार दिनों तक रहने की संभावना है. बात अगर रायपुर या मध्य छत्तीसगढ़ की करें तो शुक्रवार से बारिश से राहत मिलने की संभावना है.
एक दो जगह भारी बारिश हो सकती है
मौसम वैज्ञानिक एसके अवस्थी ने बताया कि एक साइक्लोनिक सर्कुलेशन बना हुआ है जो अगले 24 घंटे के दौरान दक्षिण उत्तर प्रदेश और उससे लगे उत्तर मध्य प्रदेश से होते हुए उत्तर पश्चिम दिशा की ओर आगे बढ़ने की संभावना है. इस प्रभाव से अगले 24 घंटे तक मध्य और उत्तर छत्तीसगढ़ के एक दो स्थानों पर गरज चमक के साथ भारी वर्षा होने की संभावना बनी हुई है. मौसम वैज्ञानिक का कहना है कि मध्य छत्तीसगढ़ में शुक्रवार से बारिश से थोड़ी राहत मिलने की संभावना है. लेकिन इसका असर सरगुजा और बिलासपुर संभाग में अगले चार दिनों तक रह सकता है.
इन जिलों में हो सकती है भारी बारिश
गुरुवार को मौसम विभाग में फिर एक बार 24 घंटे के लिए येलो अलर्ट जारी किया है. इसमें प्रदेश के बेमेतरा, गौरेला पेंड्रा मरवाही, कबीरधाम, मनेंद्रगढ़ चिरमिरी भरतपुर जिले के एक 2 स्थानों पर भारी वर्षा होने का अनुमान है.

Italy's latest heat wave is expected to continue until at least Wednesday, Sept. 9, with temperatures reaching 35°C (95°F) to 37°C (99°F) across the country, forecaster Lorenzo Tedici said Thursday, according to the ANSA News Agency.
Tedici said the heat would persist through the middle of next week as a North African high-pressure system strengthens over the Mediterranean.
"Until the middle of next week, thermometers will soar again, pushing temperatures up to 8°C (14.4°F) above the typical average for the period," he said.
He noted that cooler Atlantic air would begin moving in from Wednesday, bringing a change in weather conditions.
"Long-term mathematical models indicate a full-blown collapse of high pressure immediately after Wednesday, September 9th," Tedici said, adding that the shift would be aided by the descent of cold air from the North Atlantic.
According to the forecast, Thursday will bring sunny and warmer conditions to northern and central Italy, while the south will be mostly sunny with occasional showers in the Calabrian mountains.
On Friday, sunny and warmer conditions are expected across the country, with heat building in the north and isolated showers remaining possible in the Calabrian mountains.
Saturday is expected to stay hot, with high heat in the north and mostly sunny, warm conditions across the central and southern regions.
The long-term outlook calls for the African high-pressure system to hold, with temperatures peaking around 37°C (98.6°F) from north to south.

News summary
- The FIA has declared a Heat Hazard for the 2026 Italian Grand Prix after forecasting a heat index above 31°C during the race at Monza.
- Drivers will have to use the required cooling system or, if they choose not to wear the cooling equipment, have 0.5 kg of ballast added to the car to compensate for the difference in mass.
- It is the second Heat Hazard declaration of the 2026 F1 season, following the Austrian Grand Prix in June.
The Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) has declared a Heat Hazard for the Italian Grand Prix, which takes place at Monza from September 4-6. The decision was communicated to the teams on Thursday (3) after the governing body received a forecast from its Official Weather Service indicating that the heat index will exceed 31°C at some point during the race.
The declaration activates the heat-management procedures established in the FIA’s 2026 Sporting Regulations. Under Article B1.5.10, all components of the Driver Cooling System must be fitted to the cars for a race affected by a Heat Hazard.
Drivers may choose not to wear the personal equipment that forms part of the cooling system. In that case, however, the remaining components must still be installed and functional, while 0.5 kg of ballast must be added to the cockpit to compensate for the difference in mass between the driver’s normal personal equipment and the cooling-system equipment.
“In accordance with Article B1.5.10 of the FIA F1 Regulations, having received a forecast from the Official Weather Service predicting that the Heat Index will be greater than 31.0°C at some time during the Race at this Competition, a Heat Hazard is declared,” FIA F1 Race Director Rui Marques wrote in the notification sent to the teams on Thursday.
The FIA introduced the Heat Hazard procedure following the extreme conditions experienced at the 2023 Qatar Grand Prix, when several drivers suffered from severe heat-related symptoms. The system was introduced into the regulations for the 2025 season and was first used at the Singapore Grand Prix that year.
This is the second Heat Hazard declaration of the 2026 season. The first came ahead of the Austrian Grand Prix in June, when the FIA also activated the procedure after forecasts indicated a heat index above the 31°C threshold.
Temperatures are expected to be particularly high around Monza throughout the weekend. According to the FIA’s Official Weather Service forecast cited by Motorsport.com and Autosport, temperatures are expected to reach around 36°C during FP2 on Friday, 35°C for qualifying on Saturday and 33°C at the start of Sunday’s race.
The Italian Grand Prix is the 13th round of the 2026 Formula 1 season. The weekend begins on Friday, September 4, with FP1 and FP2, followed by FP3 and qualifying on Saturday. The race is scheduled for Sunday at 3:00 pm local time.
The GRANDE PRÊMIO will follow all the action from Monza throughout the 2026 F1 season.
FAQ
Why did the FIA declare a Heat Hazard at Monza?
The FIA’s Official Weather Service forecast a heat index above 31°C during the Italian Grand Prix, triggering Article B1.5.10 of the Sporting Regulations.
What does the Heat Hazard mean for F1 drivers?
The cars must be equipped with the components of the Driver Cooling System. Drivers can choose not to wear the cooling equipment, but in that case 0.5 kg of ballast must be added to the cockpit to compensate for the difference in mass.
How many times has the FIA used the Heat Hazard procedure in 2026?
The Italian Grand Prix marks the second Heat Hazard declaration of the 2026 season, after the procedure was also activated for the Austrian Grand Prix in June.

"WWE NXT" stars Vanity Project, the stable consisting of Jackson Drake, Brad Baylor, Ricky Smokes, and Myka Lockwood, took Heatwave by storm over the weekend when Drake captured the North American Championship from Myles Borne and Baylor and Smokes became two-time NXT Tag Team Champions. The National Meteorological Service (SMN) has issued a yellow storm alert for the City of Buenos Aires and the Buenos Aires Metropolitan Area (AMBA), highlighting Thursday, September 3 as a day of high weather instability.
The day began with difficult weather conditions, with intense rains and possible hailstorms prevailing. As time goes by, the weather is expected to gradually improve with a change of winds towards the southwest, resulting in a gradual decrease in precipitation.
Forecast for CABA and AMBA: When will the rain stop on September 3?
In the early morning and first hours of the morning, the probabilities of strong storms range between 40% and 70%. During this period, intense precipitation accompanied by frequent electrical activity and wind gusts of up to 50 km/h could be recorded.
At noon, a clear improvement in the weather is expected for CABA and the Buenos Aires suburbs. The chances of rain will drastically reduce to a range of 10% to 40%, allowing for a drier afternoon and evening with decreasing clouds.
The temperatures will range with a minimum of 14°C and a maximum of 19°C. The entry of southwest wind will bring a feeling of freshness in the last hours of the day.
In Greater Buenos Aires (GBA), water accumulation is expected to reach between 20 and 50 mm, especially in the early morning, which requires caution when traveling through areas prone to temporary flooding.
Storm alert and forecast for the weekend
The Early Warning System (SAT) of the SMN continues with the yellow storm alert for the northeast and center of Buenos Aires, Entre Ríos, and parts of Santa Fe. Intense gusts, possible hail, and electrical activity are expected before the storm system moves away towards the Atlantic Ocean.
After the rains, a mass of cold air of polar origin will bring a drop in temperatures for the rest of the week. Friday, September 4 is expected to be a sunny and cool day with temperatures between 10°C and 17°C.
With the arrival of the weekend, the cold will intensify in the central region. Saturday, September 5 will have temperatures between 8°C minimum and 14°C maximum, with partly cloudy skies.
Finally, Sunday, September 6 will record the lowest temperatures of the period in the AMBA, with a minimum of 5°C and a maximum of 13°C, consolidating a winter environment at the beginning of the next week.
